blocks.text: A full day of sport fishing off Flamingo, one of Costa Rica’s main sport-fishing centres. About 20 miles offshore, two drop-offs where the depth increases from about 110 to over 600 metres attract pelagic species such as Pacific sailfish, blue, black and striped marlin, dorado and yellowfin and bigeye tuna; around the Catalina and Brumel Islands, only 5 miles from the marina, anglers find wahoo, mackerel, jacks, snappers and the famous roosterfish. Overnight at Hotel Pasatiempo. (B, L)

blocks.text: A diving tour at the Catalina Islands, a 25-minute ride from Flamingo. Guanacaste is known for the abundance and diversity of its marine life: large schools of fish at almost every site, reef species of the Pacific and Tropical Pacific, and larger animals such as manta and eagle rays, several species of sharks, turtles and giant groupers, as well as a remarkable array of moray eels. Visibility varies from about 10 to 30 metres, depending on location, tides and currents. Overnight at Hotel Pasatiempo. (B)
